Identity.History: The Athenian Agora was the civic, commercial, and political heart of Classical Athens, serving as a marketplace, meeting place, religious center, and administrative district. Citizens gathered there to trade, debate public affairs, attend legal proceedings, worship at shrines, and conduct the daily business of the polis. Surrounded by stoas, council buildings, temples, law courts, and monuments, the Agora embodied the public life of Athenian democracy.
